If anyone recalls this post I made, then they might have this in the back of their mind somewhere.

Something is wrong in Kumon-mi right now. Even moreso than usual. And it all started in update 0.42 (the latest Beach Trip), particularly the ending of “Perfect Harmony”.

Akira was warned not to go outside, but he did anyway. When that failed, we saw Himawari show up and interact with Ayane directly. She had some kind of plan. But what? We still don’t know.

Anyway, then weird shit happened and things have been weird ever since. Everything is more… out in the open, so to speak. We’re warned multiple times afterward that “things are off”.

Not to mention the Beach is currently closed off due to a ‘tidal disaster’. Preeeetty weird.

It’s my belief that we’ll get some answers during the next Beach Trip update, as the narrator hinted at at the end of the last Reset. Sooo, update 0.52.

Maybe I’m wrong, but hey, I’m willing to stick to this belief for now if only to… lessen the sour taste that was Sana’s actions this update.

- About the Nodoka discussion… I can see what both sides of the argument are saying, but really, it’s a complicated situation. My belief is this:

I hate she did to Yumi. It was self serving and was used as a means for revenge. Revenge that Futaba, the one Nodoka was doing this for, didn’t consent to. Nodoka even admits she went overboard in this very update when questioned about it.

As for the other stuff? The stuff that revolves around breaking everyone out of their prison? Knowing her intentions, while seeing other characters hurt doesn’t make me feel good… I can understand.

It’s for the greater good. Sometimes the correct choice isn’t the most popular one, but damn y’all, someone has to do it.

Some people look at Nodoka through too broad a lense. Their perspective makes things out to be so black and white, but in reality, it’s not that simple at all.

The fact is, yes, Nodoka does things that hurt people. But only for the short term. In her mind, once she cracks the code and frees everyone? Once the truth is revealed? The ones she saved will be understanding too.

Nodoka really is all alone, or at least, she thinks she is. She’s just a teenager. A genius, yes, but a teenager nonetheless.

Once someone *cough* Akira *cough* grows the balls to finally tell her about the existence of the RAS and how others are aware of the time loops too, well then… things might become interesting.

- On a more lighthearted note, the dates with Rin and Io were really well done. Both got a kiss out of it too, so, hell yeah.

Wonder what’s up with that bottomless pit, though… Or that supposed door with a keypad for that matter. Y’know, the destination Io was planning on taking Akira to begin with?

Sounds suspicious, no? And I’m surprised no one else has talked about it. What the hell is a keypad door doing inside a cave? More and more questions to unpack…

- I’m quite looking forward to Maya’s events next update. It’s high time this version of Maya gets some genuine development. Her and Akira have been tiptoeing around each other for wayyyy too long.

- Also, goddamit Ami! Stop abusing Maya! You make it so hard to like you, but I still do for whatever fucking reason. (She’s interesting, okay?)

- More voices in Yumi’s head… I can only assume this will snowball into the wildest sex ever seen in this game when the time comes. We can’t be blueballed forever… right?

- Oh yeah. Nodokathon 2 as a whole. I didn’t like it. The footjobs were fine. I’m not a foot fetishist, but I really don’t see the problem with them. Plus I’m surprised it’s never happened in the game before.

Ami and Ayane’s threesome with Akira. Strangely hot, although I feel bad for Ayane… She seemed to get into it, though, but… who knows how much of that can be attributed to her acting skills?

Sana and Molly’s thing. Blegh. I’ve already said enough about it. I’ll be waiting for Sara’s events in 0.50. One can only imagine what fresh hell we’ll be in for. Especially since Sel said this in his AMA about Sara (it’s towards the bottom):


For the record, I disagree, Sel. Yumi is amazing and I will die on this hill.

- The Dorm Wars contests as a whole? Decent. Certainly far better than Sports Wars. Less Good Kid too! Although I don’t mind their music overall, it doesn’t fit when reading a VN.

- Yasu looked cute this update. This needed addressing.

- That is all.

Finally had some time to sleep and let the update soak in my mind… Also just caught up on the thread.

I won’t go super in depth on eeeeverything, but I’ll touch on the highlights:

- Okay, so first of all, I’m going to address the elephant in the room: what the hell is wrong with you, Sana??

Like, dude, that’s your mother. She’s the only family you have left and she loves you more than anything!

There are so many who would envy your position, and Molly points this out too in the aftermath. No, Molly isn’t totally innocent in this either, but at the same time: Haruka isn’t her family, is a predator, and is a fully functioning adult who is well aware of what she was doing.

Sara, though? Asked by her own daughter to sleep with the man she loves to raise her grades? All while Sana knew where it was leading?

That’s really fucked up.

Also, Sana’s cool with incest now? Tf?

But y’know… This makes for an interesting segue into my next point.

-

If anyone recalls this post I made, then they might have this in the back of their mind somewhere.

Something is wrong in Kumon-mi right now. Even moreso than usual. And it all started in update 0.42 (the latest Beach Trip), particularly the ending of “Perfect Harmony”.

Akira was warned not to go outside, but he did anyway. When that failed, we saw Himawari show up and interact with Ayane directly. She had some kind of plan. But what? We still don’t know.

Anyway, then weird shit happened and things have been weird ever since. Everything is more… out in the open, so to speak. We’re warned multiple times afterward that “things are off”.

spoilers.html:
- Okay, so first of all, I’m going to address the elephant in the room: what the hell is wrong with you, Sana??

Like, dude, that’s your mother. She’s the only family you have left and she loves you more than anything!

There are so many who would envy your position, and Molly points this out too in the aftermath. No, Molly isn’t totally innocent in this either, but at the same time: Haruka isn’t her family, is a predator, and is a fully functioning adult who is well aware of what she was doing.

Sara, though? Asked by her own daughter to sleep with the man she loves to raise her grades? All while Sana knew where it was leading?

That’s really fucked up.

Also, Sana’s cool with incest now? Tf?

But y’know… This makes for an interesting segue into my next point.

-

If anyone recalls this post I made, then they might have this in the back of their mind somewhere.

Something is wrong in Kumon-mi right now. Even moreso than usual. And it all started in update 0.42 (the latest Beach Trip), particularly the ending of “Perfect Harmony”.

Akira was warned not to go outside, but he did anyway. When that failed, we saw Himawari show up and interact with Ayane directly. She had some kind of plan. But what? We still don’t know.

Anyway, then weird shit happened and things have been weird ever since. Everything is more… out in the open, so to speak. We’re warned multiple times afterward that “things are off”.

Not to mention the Beach is currently closed off due to a ‘tidal disaster’. Preeeetty weird.

It’s my belief that we’ll get some answers during the next Beach Trip update, as the narrator hinted at at the end of the last Reset. Sooo, update 0.52.

Maybe I’m wrong, but hey, I’m willing to stick to this belief for now if only to… lessen the sour taste that was Sana’s actions this update.

- About the Nodoka discussion… I can see what both sides of the argument are saying, but really, it’s a complicated situation. My belief is this:

I hate she did to Yumi. It was self serving and was used as a means for revenge. Revenge that Futaba, the one Nodoka was doing this for, didn’t consent to. Nodoka even admits she went overboard in this very update when questioned about it.

As for the other stuff? The stuff that revolves around breaking everyone out of their prison? Knowing her intentions, while seeing other characters hurt doesn’t make me feel good… I can understand.

It’s for the greater good. Sometimes the correct choice isn’t the most popular one, but damn y’all, someone has to do it.

Some people look at Nodoka through too broad a lense. Their perspective makes things out to be so black and white, but in reality, it’s not that simple at all.

The fact is, yes, Nodoka does things that hurt people. But only for the short term. In her mind, once she cracks the code and frees everyone? Once the truth is revealed? The ones she saved will be understanding too.

Nodoka really is all alone, or at least, she thinks she is. She’s just a teenager. A genius, yes, but a teenager nonetheless.

Once someone *cough* Akira *cough* grows the balls to finally tell her about the existence of the RAS and how others are aware of the time loops too, well then… things might become interesting.

- On a more lighthearted note, the dates with Rin and Io were really well done. Both got a kiss out of it too, so, hell yeah.

Wonder what’s up with that bottomless pit, though… Or that supposed door with a keypad for that matter. Y’know, the destination Io was planning on taking Akira to begin with?

Sounds suspicious, no? And I’m surprised no one else has talked about it. What the hell is a keypad door doing inside a cave? More and more questions to unpack…

- I’m quite looking forward to Maya’s events next update. It’s high time this version of Maya gets some genuine development. Her and Akira have been tiptoeing around each other for wayyyy too long.

- Also, goddamit Ami! Stop abusing Maya! You make it so hard to like you, but I still do for whatever fucking reason. (She’s interesting, okay?)

- More voices in Yumi’s head… I can only assume this will snowball into the wildest sex ever seen in this game when the time comes. We can’t be blueballed forever… right?

- Oh yeah. Nodokathon 2 as a whole. I didn’t like it. The footjobs were fine. I’m not a foot fetishist, but I really don’t see the problem with them. Plus I’m surprised it’s never happened in the game before.

Ami and Ayane’s threesome with Akira. Strangely hot, although I feel bad for Ayane… She seemed to get into it, though, but… who knows how much of that can be attributed to her acting skills?

Sana and Molly’s thing. Blegh. I’ve already said enough about it. I’ll be waiting for Sara’s events in 0.50. One can only imagine what fresh hell we’ll be in for. Especially since Sel said this in his AMA about Sara (it’s towards the bottom):

View attachment 4810478

For the record, I disagree, Sel. Yumi is amazing and I will die on this hill.

- The Dorm Wars contests as a whole? Decent. Certainly far better than Sports Wars. Less Good Kid too! Although I don’t mind their music overall, it doesn’t fit when reading a VN.

- Yasu looked cute this update. This needed addressing.

- That is all.

I don't know if there was a point to Kirin & Miku scene, so I will simply ignore them and consider them non-important.

Ami & Ayane was weird. I was very surprised how easily everyone accepted the fact Sensei was fucking his daughter. Like it doesn't matter how desentize they are to things related to Sensei, their reaction being just "so what?" is just fucking weird. They don't question for how many years things have going on or at what age it started, if Sensei himself groomed Ami into being that obsessively obedient and sexual towards him and if maybe he is also doing the same to them. None, no questions asks, as if it didn't matter, as if things are the way they are meant to be.

When Kirin was starting to question it, Ami just says "don't you want to fuck your sister?" AS IF THAT CAN BE EQUATED. IS NOT THE FUCKING SAME, LIKE THEY DON'T EVEN KNOW OR QUESTION IF THIS HAS BEEN HAPPENING SINCE AMI WAS ON HER SINGLE DIGITS

Also Ami throughout all of this was probably thinking "it doesn't matter, at the end of the day, I'll be the sole winner". She is even more delusional than Chiaki ever was.

In any case, Ayane was also so weird during this. Like yeah she is part of RAS, and she already knew about Ami & Sensei, but for her to just accept it like that, in front of everybody, to allow herself, Sensei, and Ami to be degraded for Kirin, Miku, & Nodoka to spectate, it is just so fucking weird and out of character.

I don't understand Molly anymore. Is like seeing a skinwalker using her character model. Where is the character for which I felt so much pain and sadness during [Lavender's Green]? and for whom I felt bittersweet during her [Level One] & [Fated to Love You] chain event? and on top of that, she has the gall to then berate Sana over trying to bring Sara into this, when Molly herself knew from the beginning that Sara was going to be the one. Molly knew yet she tries to distance herself from it as if she had no agency in it.

Is like if someone is telling you they are going to murder someone and how they are going to do it, then your reaction been "cool story" & when they actually go and murder that person you say "hey, not cool bro.". You don't get to just wash your hands off and act as if it had nothing to do with you.

Sana was the cruelest of them all. She was an asshole. She knows her mother enough to understand the kind of reaction she would have.
Sana knows this would hurt Sara deeply. And yet she did it. Perhaps Nodoka had a purpose to do all of this, but Sana? it was nothing more than a sadistic game.

She sees it as a competition, and at least now she feels like she is ahead of her mother, perhaps she is even hoping her mother is even now forever out of said competition.

I think it can be very telling how little insight we got into Akira's head throughout all of these events. I think he was meant to be the main character of this event, to get a reaction out of him, to maybe not "break" him mentally, but instead for, as Nodoka put it,


To chip away at his armor. Not that so she can harm him, but to make him feel vulnerable but safe with them. Why? I don't know, perhaps to get some answers. perhaps to find how he is connected to the gods.
But she failed, the event wasn't mentally stimulating enough. So instead he simply closed off his mind, he dissociated once more.
The wrong players were present.

But then what was the point of Sara being there? Because I don't think Haruka was important at all. Nodoka was very in high spirits through the previous events, and she said Molly & Sana were the main dish. Why? Just like with Haruka, I don't think Molly was important for whatever Nodoka was planning for.

Then, was it Sara & Sana? why? why invite Sara to this random location to watch the video and live feed of Sensei fucking Sana, and for Nodoka to watch them watch that. What was the point? why not do it here where they were? and if not here, why didn't she send Sara directly to the love hotel? Why did Sensei had to blindfold himself if they were going to just end up at a love hotel?

As I was just finishing writing that last sentence, the more I think I was wrong about Sensei being the main character of Nodokathon 2. Clearly she was experimenting with something, there has to be some sort of purpose.

She was expecting something to happen, the question is, why? why so many degrees of separation? what was she trying to observe?
Perhaps her true objective was to trigger some sort of happy-esque event, and to be witness to it. Not as a participant, but like us, a viewer. Unlike Sensei, we remember the events, because we are not players, we are the reader and viewer. We ourselves cannot interfere, but we can observe and remember when Sensei and the rest can't.

Also contrary to most people, this time I am actually not mad a Nodoka. Unless she literally has hypnosis powers, she didn't really force any of the girls to do anything.

The only real victim of all of this is Sara.

I don't fault Sensei, since I consider him more immature than the girls, he has yet to grow a spine. Still a nascent soul inside an adult body.
Kirin and Miku chose to come here and stay despite the bombshell reveals
Ami is Ami.
Ayane chose to not only participate, but to degrade herself, Ami, & Sensei for everyone to watch, like circus animals.
Molly knew everything and still chose to participate.
And Sana? she is obviously the worst perpetrator here.


Honestly if everyone's parameters were altered during the last beach as some of you have theorize, then I hope it gets reverted back soon. Half because I miss the characters I grew to love since v0.1, and the other half because the story is simply not the same without the spice. It is so fucking boring, just a fucking snoozefest one after another.

get rid of this kumba-fucking-ya bullshit of "hehe we all love Sensei and he loves us so lets share him" or "oh Sensei is fucking his niece? so what?". I WANT THE DRAMA AND TERROR BACK.

Back in the day when one event and/or reveal was so nail-bitting, that I would dread having to press the space button to find out what was gonna happen.

I was gonna write some more about my last topic, but it has been 2 hours since I started this comment, so good night

Ami is Ami.

posts.content_html_raw:
Though I do wish to never see another Nodokathon ever gain, there ARE more things done right in Nodokathon2 compared to the first one (alas, there are also plenty of things that remain stupid...)

1. A meaningful experiment needs a clear outcome, a YES or NO. The result doesn't have to be "as expected", but it cannot be "inconclusive". Nodokathon1 hid all that behind content wall and did not tell you jack shit, but Nodokathon2 clearly demonstrates that what Nodoka has in mind this time doesn't work.

2. Nodoka's intention is more characterized and confirmed now. We don't need to guess, find excuses for her, or pretend that Nodokathons really mean something anymore: Nodoka indeed wants to break the script or at least challenge this world, presumably by trying to trigger some divine intervention via destroying (what she assumes to be) the basic principles of this strange world.

3. Nodoka's subsequent upset about Nodokathon2. It gives a little bit of humanity back to her. It might be wishful thinking that she was upset about ruining people for nothing instead of simply about a failed experiment. Regardless, anything that wipes the smug smile off her face is a good start.
1. What most of us are complaining about: how does this scene come into being and how does that and everyone's action make any sense?

I've given up on fathoming reasons for attendees, but at least this time, 3 of them are returning degenerates who haven't been personally hurt by Nodoka, 1 is an idiot too curious about sex for her own good, 1 is out of concern, and 1 is a psychopath. So it's kinda ok. Even their attitudes (or the lack of) when being forced to know about Arawaka family's ugly secret is something now I can just let it slide. NSFW logic FTW.

Still, there is still something stupid and the stupidest part this time is Sensei. He is someone who experienced being an unwilling participant of Nodoka's scheme, someone who does not like what is going on at the very beginning, someone who can tell Ayane that he really loves and appreciates her and LATER THAT NIGHT fucks his daughter right in front of her, and someone who just "yea blindfold me to somewhere so I can keep fucking things". The fact that he doesn't just walk away at the very beginning implies that either Nodoka's plot device aura is too strong for any common sense to fight it, him being extremely incapable of thinking or unwilling to ponder what might happen, or Kirin's grandma socks are simply too alluring to refuse.

2. Her experiment design is improved but something somewhere still feels very flawed.
- Unless the first two contests are purely for making the mood and coercing Sensei into participating the third important one without too much resisting, Miku x Kirin and Ayane x Ami in actuality mean literally nothing from the looks of it. In fact, her whole experiment would've felt a lot better imo if it's cut to just Molly x Sana. Torturing Ayane throughout this session feels absolutely unnecessary and meaningless.
(Moreover, the whole Nodokathon2 would've been infinitely better if she actually triggered something but everything got quickly course-corrected so that no one except reviewer remembered that)

- Nodoka's objective can still use some work. "If I say it, you'd think I am crazy." is now far from satisfying for us hungry viewers. C'mom Selly! We've had so much of your hallucinogenic vomit now that I am sure we can all handle Nodoka's shit if you're ever willing to let her come clean. You can't let her hide from garbage made of words forever and let her value continuously drop in the meantime.

- Nodoka's approach toward her objective needs a lot of work. Namely, answer the same set of questions I'd throw at both Nodokathon1 and Nodokathon2: Why do you think all-female sexfest or revealing truths to side characters (or devastating them) would work for whatever you've planned for? What part of the entire Nodokathon2 is really what you think to presumably be the key? What is the rationale behind it? Why do you pick these when there are literally infinite ways but technically no way for a character to break out of its script? I understand that these might just be extremely major spoilers and cannot be revealed too easily. But I really don't what to see Nodoka seeming trying random things then getting dubious results and we have to believe that it means more than what is on paper because we aren't allowed to know more.
1. Nodoka will give up on her experiment if Sensei didn't have sex with Sara, Haruka, or Ami. What a mighty obstacle that even our genius can't even go around!
Guh! Gotta have to delay my plan of figuring out Kumon-mi and understanding Kyoko's words now all because you don't sex Sara, Sensei! You goddamn coward!

2. The "cloud" background at the end of this dorm wars is independent of Nodokathon2; it just looks fucky with no apparent reason.

(Usually my posts are structured, so mind that this one is just a very big ramble. Some of the points I raise may be interesting, but you won't miss much by skipping it.)
I've been kind of silent because tbh I was underwhelmed by the update. Not on what happened, but on the quality of writing overall. And I'm still making my mind on how to look at the game from here on. Well, I'll be echoing many complaints that I have seen already:
The first ten events felt very off to me, like Selebus couldn't decide if he was still on the FanFest or not. The music didn't fit most of the time, and on my notes there is "BORING" as a commentary multiple times. It's like he can't decide if he's going to take this seriously (with Imani figuring out he is banging everyone and she's now also guilty for not reporting and enabling it), or it's just fantasy land with her mysteriously accepting that on day two there will be no Akira, for whatever reason.

Furthermore, it's still weird for Imani to accept being side chick to Niki, when Akira's living with her and Ami refers to her as mom. It's like, really, dude? Aren't you an adult? It's one thing for teenagers to behave like this, but Imani basically willingly put herself in the position of "homewrecker" of her own volition - which yeah, I guess Akira has now a black (the only in the game) woman sidechick that he only uses for sex and has absolutely no intention of having any future whatsoever with. Maybe that's a commentary on something.

But Imani has nothing to do with my complaint, that was just my ramble. What I mean about it feeling off is that it goes from Imani being stupid or faking stupidity about the second day, to an actual death ball discovering lesbianism and ascending from this plane of existence, amidst our characters seeing themselves in a documentary from the future (...) it's like, this is absolutely 100% fanfest. It's just idiotic that this is part of the canon now.

Then we get to Io's event, which is a mini episode of stranger things with them stumbling onto a hole in the middle of a trek/tunnel/journey - which might be acceptable, were not for the very death ball discovering lesbianism while sharing the screen with a crocodile wearing a hat that came just before. The Io thing could have been taken seriously, but how do I take it seriously when it just came from an absolute circus of an event?

Then we have Rin's event, which is pretty much the one sane event of this update. Where things, you know, actually make sense UNTIL Akira decides that now he'll address the reader, because why the fuck not. Use your hand to break the fourth wall and block our view of the camera (???). When was that a thing? It was never a thing, and it will never be a thing, because it's yet again, Selebus writing whatever the hell he thought of first and lacking an editor.

Then we go to Nodokathon II, which is one of the most verbose and unnecessary pieces of writings ever. The entire update is btw, but my god, Selebus went on ranting about having written so much as if he deserved a reward, and guess what, he should have written less.

Anyway, rant over. Here's the summary of my current feelings: The FanFest has clearly affected Selebus' writing in a bad way. He lost touch of the tone and pacing of his story, which resulted in the first ten events of the update being off. There are good moments in almost all of them, but they lack refinement. I hope he takes a month to rest and gets his head on the right track again.
Now, I'd like to take a step back from the update itself and reflect a bit on what's going on storywise, because I feel that the schedule has skewed our perception of the big picture in some ways:
So, let's recap a bit of what's happening: Akira is useless as always and, honestly, has become quite pathetic, not only as himself, but also as someone to be watched. The Christmas thing really drove that point home with him behaving as either a walking dildo for the girls or someone that belongs in a mental institution. Selebus has got to go somewhere with his development because it's starting to drag something fierce.

It's also becoming clear that Selebus is taking steps to drive the story to the harem end. Everyone has to be aware of everyone, and everyone has to have sex with him."How do I make all these characters have sex with Akira and find out about eachother in an interest manner?" is the driving force of the story now.

So every girl knows his name is Akira, the mothers have to find out about their daughters (Nodokathon II), the characters that weren't interested have to become so (Rika/Yumi/Tsuneyo/Karin). You can see that he created events to make them have no choice but to go this path. Rika was holding back but then is forced to come on to him because of Rin, Yumi's because of fearing Yuki's death, Tsuneyo because Sekai dream rapes her, Karin is convinced by Touka that his episode was out of his control.

Sana's situation is quite peculiar though, because she's just lost. However, the degree to which she's lost is now linked to the green path. Her and Molly only pull out the invite if Akira has been having sex with Ami, Sara and Haruka. All three. Which means that realistically nothing can come out of this, there are just way too many possible paths.

And yet, Selebus has to somehow work his path towards the revelation of Sara's past. This coming from watching Akira have a threesome with Sana and Molly makes complete sense. But how do you keep the revelation if it comes from nothing? When Nodoka blackmailed Yumi, it was possible for the paths to converge because it was a matter of degree of assault. When Stomachache happened, it was also a matter of degree - the fight always happens, it's the ending that is different.

This, however, is FOUR missed events, of which only the last one is the Sana/Sara stuff. Which means that there's no ending point to reconnect from. In the green path something very traumatic happens, and on the red path NOTHING, absolutely nothing happens. Sana wasn't even there, much less Sara. It's clear to me that other than Himawari's plan, the Sara's past revelation is the big deal of the chapter - but now I wonder how Selebus will manage to pull this off in both paths, and if it will make even clearer that LiL shouldn't ever have had multiple paths (as they are).
Anyway, I think the healthiest path forward is dismissing the entire update as something that ought to be thought about. Maybe in the future its status as a weird fever dream will get diluted by (one hopes) better pieces of writing before and after. Rather than a single bizarre update consumed on its own.

Edit: Eventually I may address each individual event, but honestly I'm just having more fun on my second playthrough of TLS than engaging with it for a second time. Never before have I thought about stopping playing LiL, but it did happen during 0.49.

Sana's situation is quite peculiar though, because she's just lost. However, the degree to which she's lost is now linked to the green path. Her and Molly only pull out the invite if Akira has been having sex with Ami, Sara and Haruka. All three. Which means that realistically nothing can come out of this, there are just way too many possible paths.

And yet, Selebus has to somehow work his path towards the revelation of Sara's past. This coming from watching Akira have a threesome with Sana and Molly makes complete sense. But how do you keep the revelation if it comes from nothing? When Nodoka blackmailed Yumi, it was possible for the paths to converge because it was a matter of degree of assault. When Stomachache happened, it was also a matter of degree - the fight always happens, it's the ending that is different.

This, however, is FOUR missed events, of which only the last one is the Sana/Sara stuff. Which means that there's no ending point to reconnect from. In the green path something very traumatic happens, and on the red path NOTHING, absolutely nothing happens. Sana wasn't even there, much less Sara. It's clear to me that other than Himawari's plan, the Sara's past revelation is the big deal of the chapter - but now I wonder how Selebus will manage to pull this off in both paths, and if it will make even clearer that LiL shouldn't ever have had multiple paths (as they are).
Anyway, I think the healthiest path forward is dismissing the entire update as something that ought to be thought about. Maybe in the future its status as a weird fever dream will get diluted by (one hopes) better pieces of writing before and after. Rather than a single bizarre update consumed on its own.

Edit: Eventually I may address each individual event, but honestly I'm just having more fun on my second playthrough of TLS than engaging with it for a second time. Never before have I thought about stopping playing LiL, but it did happen during 0.49.

spoilers.title: general thoughts about the update
spoilers.html:
I've been kind of silent because tbh I was underwhelmed by the update. Not on what happened, but on the quality of writing overall. And I'm still making my mind on how to look at the game from here on. Well, I'll be echoing many complaints that I have seen already:
The first ten events felt very off to me, like Selebus couldn't decide if he was still on the FanFest or not. The music didn't fit most of the time, and on my notes there is "BORING" as a commentary multiple times. It's like he can't decide if he's going to take this seriously (with Imani figuring out he is banging everyone and she's now also guilty for not reporting and enabling it), or it's just fantasy land with her mysteriously accepting that on day two there will be no Akira, for whatever reason.

Furthermore, it's still weird for Imani to accept being side chick to Niki, when Akira's living with her and Ami refers to her as mom. It's like, really, dude? Aren't you an adult? It's one thing for teenagers to behave like this, but Imani basically willingly put herself in the position of "homewrecker" of her own volition - which yeah, I guess Akira has now a black (the only in the game) woman sidechick that he only uses for sex and has absolutely no intention of having any future whatsoever with. Maybe that's a commentary on something.

But Imani has nothing to do with my complaint, that was just my ramble. What I mean about it feeling off is that it goes from Imani being stupid or faking stupidity about the second day, to an actual death ball discovering lesbianism and ascending from this plane of existence, amidst our characters seeing themselves in a documentary from the future (...) it's like, this is absolutely 100% fanfest. It's just idiotic that this is part of the canon now.

Then we get to Io's event, which is a mini episode of stranger things with them stumbling onto a hole in the middle of a trek/tunnel/journey - which might be acceptable, were not for the very death ball discovering lesbianism while sharing the screen with a crocodile wearing a hat that came just before. The Io thing could have been taken seriously, but how do I take it seriously when it just came from an absolute circus of an event?

Then we have Rin's event, which is pretty much the one sane event of this update. Where things, you know, actually make sense UNTIL Akira decides that now he'll address the reader, because why the fuck not. Use your hand to break the fourth wall and block our view of the camera (???). When was that a thing? It was never a thing, and it will never be a thing, because it's yet again, Selebus writing whatever the hell he thought of first and lacking an editor.

Then we go to Nodokathon II, which is one of the most verbose and unnecessary pieces of writings ever. The entire update is btw, but my god, Selebus went on ranting about having written so much as if he deserved a reward, and guess what, he should have written less.

Anyway, rant over. Here's the summary of my current feelings: The FanFest has clearly affected Selebus' writing in a bad way. He lost touch of the tone and pacing of his story, which resulted in the first ten events of the update being off. There are good moments in almost all of them, but they lack refinement. I hope he takes a month to rest and gets his head on the right track again.
Now, I'd like to take a step back from the update itself and reflect a bit on what's going on storywise, because I feel that the schedule has skewed our perception of the big picture in some ways:
So, let's recap a bit of what's happening: Akira is useless as always and, honestly, has become quite pathetic, not only as himself, but also as someone to be watched. The Christmas thing really drove that point home with him behaving as either a walking dildo for the girls or someone that belongs in a mental institution. Selebus has got to go somewhere with his development because it's starting to drag something fierce.

It's also becoming clear that Selebus is taking steps to drive the story to the harem end. Everyone has to be aware of everyone, and everyone has to have sex with him."How do I make all these characters have sex with Akira and find out about eachother in an interest manner?" is the driving force of the story now.

So every girl knows his name is Akira, the mothers have to find out about their daughters (Nodokathon II), the characters that weren't interested have to become so (Rika/Yumi/Tsuneyo/Karin). You can see that he created events to make them have no choice but to go this path. Rika was holding back but then is forced to come on to him because of Rin, Yumi's because of fearing Yuki's death, Tsuneyo because Sekai dream rapes her, Karin is convinced by Touka that his episode was out of his control.

Sana's situation is quite peculiar though, because she's just lost. However, the degree to which she's lost is now linked to the green path. Her and Molly only pull out the invite if Akira has been having sex with Ami, Sara and Haruka. All three. Which means that realistically nothing can come out of this, there are just way too many possible paths.

And yet, Selebus has to somehow work his path towards the revelation of Sara's past. This coming from watching Akira have a threesome with Sana and Molly makes complete sense. But how do you keep the revelation if it comes from nothing? When Nodoka blackmailed Yumi, it was possible for the paths to converge because it was a matter of degree of assault. When Stomachache happened, it was also a matter of degree - the fight always happens, it's the ending that is different.

This, however, is FOUR missed events, of which only the last one is the Sana/Sara stuff. Which means that there's no ending point to reconnect from. In the green path something very traumatic happens, and on the red path NOTHING, absolutely nothing happens. Sana wasn't even there, much less Sara. It's clear to me that other than Himawari's plan, the Sara's past revelation is the big deal of the chapter - but now I wonder how Selebus will manage to pull this off in both paths, and if it will make even clearer that LiL shouldn't ever have had multiple paths (as they are).

I didn't think that she would even be an option, since it feels like the game has been trying to force a different girl on Akira the entire time. I was pleasantly surprised.
Maya
is honestly the least desirable girl in this entire game aside from the wizards IMO, so that was kind of annoying. Maybe that's the point, Sel tries to poke people constantly.
Click to expand...
Ayane's had a decent amount of a sort of... 'underlying' appearance recently tbh, like she comes up in places you wouldn't expect.

I've got my own sort of "Sensei winners ranking" in my head and I keep finding myself bumping Ayane up over time.

As for Maya I actually quite like her, obviously this 'iteration' of her is miles weaker than the one we got to know through seasons 1 - 3 but I think watching her try and find herself could be a very interesting story and I like that she's opening up quickly to things we wouldn't expect.
I do hope we got OG Maya back though, whether its just a case of her remembering or whether its an alternate universe thing I can't say.

Stomache wasn't even that long ago but it was well done, and IOs first kiss is adorable.
Yumi's recent events have almost all been bangars, and I love Touka as a whole.

I worry we brigade the "quality" of the writing just because there's an event or two we don't like.
Until we get to a point where nothing is well written for an extended period I won't call it a degradation myself, especially cause dry spots are always going to be a thing.

posts.content_html_raw: When a story revolves around perception, identity, and reality, and how those three influence each other, it is easy to lose the suspension of disbelief for the reader. So far Sel has done a great job writing a story that deals with metaphysical reality questioning themes. I agree with Moonflare and others about this update feeling worse than Sel's standard, and for me this is largely due to my suspension of disbelief growing weak from certain reactions of the characters in this update. In a narrative with a fluid sense of reality, the character's identities have to contain a certian level a nuance, and I feel like this update in particular simplified characters rather than build upon their nuance. My suspension of disbelief isn't shattered yet, I feel like how good/bad this update is hinges on what happens immediately after in .5, but I fear that certain aspects of this update will be ignored when they need to not be. Update reminds me a lot of Heavenly Delusion for those who have seen it, and I'm not too big of a fan with how that manga/anime spent little time on the immediate aftermath of its most notable traumatic incident.

Recently, especially in this update, the only indications we have that characters aren't quite there is what they say or do, not how. Putting a different way, how long / consistently to do you feel like your suspension of your suspension of disbelief ought to be? How long does the reader have to suspend their suspension of disbelief before the essence or meaning of LiL changes completely? Just because everything in this update makes sense with the rules Sel gives us doesn't mean it's as impactful. Past turmoil was both heavy hitting and well placed, the weight of the narrative blow hits hard, but this update contains heavy content without the expert placement that events like Stomachache has, and I would argue it's due to the lack of visceral on screen reaction from participants and bystanders, not the plot beat itself. A heavy punch that grazes this update is, not a knockout punch like past climactic events.
